messages:
maya: FYI Acme reported intermittent 403s after we rotated service keys last night. They ran a curl repro that sometimes succeeds and sometimes 403s. Putting the bits here so we can collect request IDs and a debug bundle.

sam: Thanks — can you paste the curl they ran + any request IDs from their response headers? Also which org/project the failures are against?

maya: Customer sent this minimal repro (token redacted):
```
curl -v \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_****' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-big","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```
They say ~20% of requests return 403. One 403 response header they captured: `x-request-id: rq_20260317_1a2b3c`, `x-response-code: 403`.

arjun: Do we know whether the token they used is a project-scoped service key or an org-scoped key? Rotation could have left a stale mapping if we swapped key IDs.

maya: They said it was a service key tied to project `acme-prod` but also tried an org-wide token and saw the same flakiness. They rotated keys at 2026-03-17T03:12:00Z.

sre-jordan: Can you paste the gateway logs for that x-request-id? If it's signature/auth, logs usually show something like `auth: signed-claim-mismatch` or `auth: key-not-found`.

maya: From our edge logs for rq_20260317_1a2b3c: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:25:12Z] INFO req=rq_20260317_1a2b3c src=gw01 auth=FAIL reason="signed-claim-mismatch" key_id="k_OLD_7f3"
[2026-03-17T03:25:12Z] DEBUG req=rq_20260317_1a2b3c token_sub=service:acme-prod proj=acme-prod org=org_acme
[2026-03-17T03:25:12Z] INFO req=rq_20260317_1a2b3c response=403 route=/v1/generate
```
They also have a success request id: `rq_20260317_2b3c4d` with edge log: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:26:01Z] INFO req=rq_20260317_2b3c4d src=gw02 auth=OK key_id="k_NEW_a9f" proj=acme-prod org=org_acme
[2026-03-17T03:26:01Z] INFO req=rq_20260317_2b3c4d response=200 route=/v1/generate
```

sam: That looks like a classic key rotation race: some gateways still resolving old signing key metadata to k_OLD_7f3. We need the full debug bundle from their environment and the request headers from the failing attempts. Ask them to capture the raw response (headers + body) for one failing and one succeeding call and to upload a debug bundle.

maya: I asked them to run: 
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_****' -H 'X-Org: org_acme' -H 'X-Project: acme-prod' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-big","input":"hello"}'
```
and to save both outputs. Also requested their debug bundle using our support script: 
```
curl -sS https://support.redwood-inference.com/debug-agent.sh | bash -s -- --collect-headers --include-curl
# yields debug bundle id: dbundle_<id>
```

support-bot: Debug bundle created: dbundle_1756123499_01 (uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/dbundle_1756123499_01.tar.gz).

arjun: Good — can they also include the client time skew, environment (k8s nodes), and whether they're hitting a load balancer or a NAT that might reuse connections? If the old key mapping is cached in some gateway instances, connection reuse could hit mixed states.

sam: On our side: I've kicked a cache invalidation for key metadata across gateways and pushed a coordinated restart to gw01. If they still see 403s after that, collect request IDs and we can trace them to specific gateway instances.

maya: I told the customer to give us two failing x-request-ids and the debug bundle link. They responded with `rq_20260317_1a2b3c` (fail) and `rq_20260317_2b3c4d` (success) and uploaded dbundle_1756123499_01. Link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-debug/dbundle_1756123499_01.tar.gz

sre-jordan: I'll pull the bundle and correlate timestamps. Also check whether the rotated key's public metadata propagated to all key servers. If we see `key_id="k_OLD_7f3"` in the failing auth attempts, likely some gateway still has stale key->kid mapping.

arjun: When you open the bundle, grep for `Authorization` / `x-request-id` and for `key_id`. If needed, instruct the customer to re-run a failing request with `-H 'X-Debug: 1'` so the edge echoes the resolved key_id in a header (we can temporarily enable for support sessions).

maya: Customer will re-run with X-Debug and post results. They said thanks and will come back in ~30m. :thumbsup:

sam: Followup checklist for us: 1) confirm cache invalidation succeeded across all gateways, 2) correlate rq_ ids to instance logs, 3) verify rotation job didn't leave an orphan mapping, 4) confirm no scope mismatch between org/project claims.

sre-jordan: On it. I'll update this thread when I confirm the gateway state or have a trace for rq_20260317_1a2b3c.

maya: marking as P1 until we confirm no more flaps.
